sections.title: Level 2 Strategy for Age Problems
sections.content: In Level 2, questions often involve average age, multiple time periods, and data correction. Step 1: Assume present ages as variables. Step 2: Adjust ages according to the time shift (past or future). Step 3: Form equations using average or ratio conditions. Step 4: Solve the equations and verify that the values satisfy the given conditions.

sections.title: Average Age Concept
sections.content: Average age = Total ages / Number of persons. Step 1: Convert the average into total age. Step 2: If time changes, add or subtract those years to each person's age. Step 3: Adjust the total age when a new person joins or someone leaves. Example: If the average age of husband and wife is 25, then total age = 25 × 2 = 50.

sections.title: Average Age with New Member
sections.content: Step 1: Find total age using the initial average. Step 2: Increase each person's age when years pass. Step 3: When a new member (such as a child) joins, add their age to the total age. Step 4: Form an equation using the new average. Example: After 5 years of marriage, the total age of husband and wife becomes 50 + 10 = 60.

sections.title: Multi-Period Ratio Problems
sections.content: Step 1: Assume the present ages of all persons as variables. Step 2: Add or subtract years for past and future ages. Step 3: Form equations according to the given ratios. Step 4: Solve all equations to determine the ages. Example: The ratio 10 years ago and the ratio 8 years later may be different.

sections.title: Erroneous Data / Correction Method
sections.content: Step 1: Find the initial total age using the incorrect average or age. Step 2: Determine the difference between the incorrect and correct values. Step 3: Adjust the total age accordingly. Step 4: Calculate the correct average or age. Example: If someone's age was read as 30 instead of 20, there will be a difference of 10 in the total age.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Not converting average into total age. 2. Forgetting to adjust ages according to time changes. 3. Assuming incorrect variables in multi-person ratio problems. 4. Calculating the difference incorrectly in erroneous data questions.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2 age problems, average, ratio, and correction logic play key roles. Always convert the average into total age, adjust for time changes, and use the difference method for correction-type questions.

tricks.title: Average to Total Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Average × number of persons = total age.

tricks.title: Years Passed Trick
tricks.explanation: If there are n people and t years pass, then the total age increases by n × t.
tricks.example: 2 people, after 5 years → total age increases by 10.

tricks.title: New Member Addition
tricks.explanation: When a new person joins, add their age to the total age and increase the number of persons.
tricks.example: Total age = 60, child age = 0 → new total = 60.

tricks.title: Ratio Equation Method
tricks.explanation: Convert the ratio into fractional form to create equations.

tricks.title: Multi-Time Shift Trick
tricks.explanation: Subtract years for past ages and add years for future ages.

tricks.title: Correction Difference Method
tricks.explanation: The difference between incorrect and correct values changes the total age.

tricks.title: Quick Average Change
tricks.explanation: Average change × number of persons = total age change.
tricks.example: Average increased by 2, persons = 5 → total increase = 10.

tricks.title: Verification Trick
tricks.explanation: Substitute the final ages into past or future conditions to verify the answer.
tricks.example: Check whether the age values satisfy the given ratio condition.
